title: A Prayer for Safe Passage and for the Jews
english: “…souls of the righteous enter; no longer do the gloomy regions of death take in the spirits of the living. Following you, who became at once the firstfruits of the living and of the dead (1 Corinthians 15:20), so that you might be Lord of both the dead and the living (Romans 14:9), the whole mass of the dead takes courage, and not without reason.

‘Receive, then, my spirit’ (Acts 7:59). Do not let the hunters lie in wait for your sparrow (Psalm 124:7), nor let the enemies who meet me at the gates spoil my departure from the earth or trouble my ascent into the heavens.”
This prayer, then, he offered up for himself; but he offered up another, in turn, for the people of the Jews: “Lord, do not set this sin against them” (Acts 7:60). And…
translator_notes: Stephen's prayer, begun in the previous section, continues as far as 'into the heavens'.
φύραμα is the 'mass' or lump of dough (the image of Romans 11:16), here the whole company of the dead.
Psalm 124:7 is LXX Psalm 123:7. 'The enemies who meet me at the gates' may echo Psalm 127:5 (LXX 126:5); it is not cited inline because the echo is uncertain.
The section ends on 'And…'; the sentence continues in the next section.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctum Stephanum (Khazarzar) u02 rem early

title: The Judge Who Weighs Our Deeds
english: …here is the point: he did not say, “Do not count it against them,” but “Do not set it,” surely so that you may learn that our Judge weighs with an exact balance, weighing each person’s deeds at the time of judgment. For if “he set the mountains in a balance and the valleys on a scale” (Isaiah 40:12), how much more does he weigh what is ours, whether our failings or our good deeds?

“Do not set this sin against them” (Acts 7:60). Do not lift it onto the scale of judgment; do not weigh down, on my account, those already weighed down by their own doing; let not my blessing become for others an occasion of curse, nor my gain a cause of loss to the Jews.
I do not want my sacrifice to bring harm on those who offer it. For even if…
translator_notes: The section opens mid-sentence: Καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν ('And here is the point') follows the 'And…' that ends the previous section.

Hesychius plays on ἵστημι in Acts 7:60 ('set', also 'weigh in a balance', as in Isaiah 40:12 ἔστησεν … σταθμῷ). 'Set' is kept in both quotations, here and in the previous section, so the wordplay survives.
'Do not count it against them' (Μὴ λογίσῃ αὐτοῖς) is Hesychius's hypothetical alternative wording, not a quotation; it may echo Psalm 32:2 (LXX 31:2) or 2 Corinthians 5:19, so no inline citation.
From 'Do not lift it onto the scale' the words are Hesychius's expansion of Stephen's prayer in Stephen's own voice; the first person continues into the next section.
θύουσιν ('those who offer it') has no expressed object; the sacrifice is Stephen himself. The section ends mid-sentence at Εἰ γὰρ καί.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctum Stephanum (Khazarzar) u02 rem mid

title: Blood Poured Out in Confession
english: …they offer it with wicked intent, still I respect them, for even against their own purpose they are for me the occasion of coming into your presence, of the kingdom of heaven, of release from the clay, of being taken up on high, of a martyr’s victory, of confessing you and being confessed by you.

For yours is the voice that speaks to us; urged on by it, I readily gave myself up to sacrifice and, through my confession, poured out my blood into your hands as into a bowl: “Everyone who confesses me before men, I also will confess him before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10:32). To him be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
translator_notes: The section opens mid-sentence: Εἰ γὰρ καί ('For even if…') ends the previous section. Stephen's first-person prayer, as Hesychius voices it, continues.
αἰσχύνομαι with the accusative means 'feel shame before, stand in awe of, respect' (LSJ); 'respect' chosen because Stephen honours his killers as the unwilling occasion of his crown.

ὁμολογίας τῆς εἰς σὲ καὶ παρὰ σοῦ: literally 'the confession toward you and from you'; it points ahead to Matthew 10:32 (the martyr confesses Christ, and Christ confesses the martyr), so rendered 'of confessing you and being confessed by you'.
κρατήρ is a mixing bowl; 'bowl' keeps the image without adding a eucharistic 'chalice'. Αὐτῷ in the doxology refers to Christ.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctum Stephanum (Khazarzar) u02 rem close
